Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The failing test org.apache.commons.math3.linear.SparseRealVectorTest.testEbeDivideMixedTypes() is related to the method ebeDivide of OpenMapRealVector. The current bug report points out issues in both ebeMultiply and ebeDivide when one of the entries in the specified RealVector is NaN or infinity.

Examining the implementation of ebeMultiply shows a potential issue asserted in comments (lines 368-370). The method assumes 0 multiplied by any x is 0, and thus only iterates over the non-zero entries of the current vector (this). This results in ignoring the case where this[i] = 0 and v[i] = NaN or infinity, which by IEEE floating-point arithmetic, should propagate NaN or infinity rather than produce zero. The current implementation does not handle these edge cases beyond the comment acknowledgement.

In the method ebeDivide, the comment at lines 345-347 mentions that it is not sufficient to loop only through the non-zero entries of this, since 0/0 = NaN should be reflected correctly. The code below iterates only over non-zero entries (line 349-353), setting res entries based on this value divided by the corresponding v entry. However, it does not handle any non-zero entries in v at indices where this entry is zero (these would be skipped entirely, missing potential NaN or infinity results in output).

Both methods share the flaw of iterating only over the entries of the original vector, ignoring the entries in v that could cause NaN or Infinity results at indices where this vector has zero entries. This leads to incorrect results when the input vector v has NaN or Infinity at indices where this vector has zero.

Therefore, the root cause of the bug is that ebeMultiply and ebeDivide in OpenMapRealVector only iterate over non-zero entries of the current vector and do not consider the entire dimension vector to properly propagate NaN or infinity values resulting from operations involving zero entries combined with NaN or Infinity in the argument RealVector.

No recent bug reports seem directly related to this numeric edge case in vector element-wise operations.

The solution should involve modifying these methods to consider all indices or at least handle special cases where the current vector's entries are zero but the input vector's entries are NaN, Infinity, or zero (for division). They must ensure correct IEEE behavior for such mixed cases.

Best methods to fix: OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply(RealVector), OpenMapRealVector.ebeDivide(RealVector)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
